features: THE F24 TAX CODE IS NO LONGER INVENTED — When a supplier had no recipient nature on file, the F24 form was still prepared, silently using code 1019: the code for individuals, printed even on a limited company, which requires 1020. The money reached the Revenue Agency under a code that was not its own, and fixing that means dealing with the Agency, not writing a journal entry. The program now stops and names the supplier. It was found in the demo building, where the form really did carry 1019 for an s.r.l.

YOU FIND OUT WHEN YOU OPEN THE PAGE, NOT WHEN YOU PRESS THE BUTTON — Above the withholding schedule there is now a list of the suppliers missing their recipient nature, each linking straight to its own record: the fix is one click instead of a hunt through every supplier paid in the period. While that list is there, the «Update deadlines» button stays disabled and says why — so there is a single message, and it arrives before the action instead of after it.

ASKED ONLY WHERE IT DECIDES SOMETHING — The recipient nature changes the tax code for one regime only, the 4% contract withholding: 1019 for income-tax individuals, 1020 for corporation-tax entities. For self-employment, commissions and non-residents the code is always 1040, and for employment always 1001. Anyone paying only a professional is therefore no longer stopped over a field that would not change a thing on their form.

THE SUPPLIER RECORD ASKS WHEN IT MATTERS, WITHOUT BLOCKING OLD DATA — Creating a contract supplier, switching the withholding flag on, or touching the tax panel now makes the recipient nature mandatory, with a message that says why and not merely that it is missing. A record already on file and already incomplete can still be saved while you are changing something else — the IBAN, the phone number: inherited gaps are caught by the F24 check, at the moment the data is actually needed.

A REJECTION CAN NO LONGER BE SILENT — In the window that creates a supplier from the XML file, errors were shown field by field, and a rejection on an unlisted field simply put the button back with no message at all. Anything without a place under its own field now appears at the top of the window.

DUE DATE AND TAX CODE IN LINE WITH THE REST — In the F24 schedule the date with its countdown, and the tax code, took two lines while the other columns took one, so the table read like a staircase. They now sit on a single line, and the tax code is a chip like the payment type instead of monospaced text.
